revealWordProblem.title: Apply: The Sealed Vault
revealWordProblem.text: Detective Ortiz found a 7/8-yard length of security cable at the crime scene. Forensics needs to cut it into 1/16-yard pieces to test each segment for fingerprints. How many 1/16-yard pieces can she cut from the cable? Show your division equation and explain your reasoning.
revealWordProblem.sampleAnswer: Ortiz needs to find how many 1/16-yard pieces fit into the 7/8-yard cable, so the dividend is 7/8 and the divisor is 1/16: 7/8 ÷ 1/16. Keep 7/8, change ÷ to ×, and flip the divisor 1/16 to its reciprocal 16/1: 7/8 × 16/1 = 112/8 = 14. The quotient 14 is already simplified, so Ortiz can cut 14 pieces of security cable, each 1/16 yard long.

conceptIntro.heading: How do I divide one fraction by another fraction?
conceptIntro.intro: When you divide a fraction by a fraction, you keep the first fraction, change ÷ to ×, and flip the second fraction (the divisor) to its reciprocal. Then multiply and simplify.
conceptIntro.keyIdea: To divide fractions, multiply the first by the reciprocal of the second, then simplify. A mixed number has to become an improper fraction BEFORE that happens.

iDo.title: Watch me
lines: Agent Rivera has 3/4 pound and each portion is 1/8 pound. I want 3/4 ÷ 1/8.
Keep 3/4. Change ÷ to ×. Flip the divisor 1/8 to its reciprocal 8/1.
Simplify: 24/4 = 6. So 3/4 ÷ 1/8 = 6. She can make 6 portions.

weDo.title: Let's try together
lines: Let's try 1/2 ÷ 1/4. Keep 1/2, change to ×, flip 1/4 to 4/1.

youDo.title: Your turn — a mixed number this time
lines: Try 2 1/2 ÷ 1/4. The first number is a mixed number, so it cannot be flipped or multiplied as it stands.
Rewrite it as an improper fraction: 2 1/2 = 5/2, because two wholes are 4 halves plus 1 more half.
Simplify: 20/2 = 10. So 2 1/2 ÷ 1/4 = 10 — check that it is reasonable, since many quarter-pieces fit into two and a half wholes.

optional.instructions: Lock 5 — Sort each cracked code: is the quotient a WHOLE NUMBER or NOT a whole number?
optional.hint: For each expression, determine whether dividing by the fraction makes the answer bigger or smaller.
optional.explanation: A quotient is a whole number only when the divisor fits into the dividend an exact number of times. 3/8 ÷ 1/8 = 3, 5/8 ÷ 1/8 = 5, and 1/2 ÷ 1/8 = 4 count whole eighth-size pieces, while 7/10 ÷ 1/5 = 7/2, 3/4 ÷ 1/2 = 3/2, and 1/3 ÷ 2/3 = 1/2 each end with a leftover part of a piece, so those codes stay fractions.
optional.explanationEs: Un cociente es un número entero solo cuando el divisor cabe en el dividendo una cantidad exacta de veces. 3/8 ÷ 1/8 = 3, 5/8 ÷ 1/8 = 5 y 1/2 ÷ 1/8 = 4 cuentan piezas completas de un octavo, mientras que 7/10 ÷ 1/5 = 7/2, 3/4 ÷ 1/2 = 3/2 y 1/3 ÷ 2/3 = 1/2 terminan con una parte sobrante de una pieza, así que esos códigos siguen siendo fracciones.

approaching.title: Spot the Common Mistake
approaching.correctWork: The student tried to divide the tops and bottoms straight across instead of using Keep, Change, Flip. Keep 1/2, change ÷ to ×, and flip the divisor 1/4 to 4/1: 1/2 × 4/1 = 4/2 = 2. (Even though the answer happens to be 2 here, dividing straight across is not a reliable rule — it breaks for problems like 2/3 ÷ 1/2.)
hints: You cannot divide fractions by dividing the numerators and denominators straight across.
Use Keep, Change, Flip: keep 1/2, change ÷ to ×, and flip the divisor 1/4 to its reciprocal 4/1.
approaching.explanation: In the second step the numerators and denominators were divided straight across, which is not how fraction division works. Keep 1/2, change ÷ to ×, and flip the divisor 1/4 to 4/1: 1/2 × 4/1 = 4/2 = 2. The answer happens to match here, but straight-across dividing falls apart on a problem like 2/3 ÷ 1/2.
approaching.explanationEs: En el segundo paso se dividieron los numeradores y los denominadores en línea recta, y así no funciona la división de fracciones. Conserva 1/2, cambia ÷ por × y voltea el divisor 1/4 para obtener 4/1: 1/2 × 4/1 = 4/2 = 2. Aquí la respuesta coincide por casualidad, pero dividir en línea recta falla en un problema como 2/3 ÷ 1/2.
approaching.correctWorkEs: El estudiante intentó dividir los numeradores y denominadores directamente en lugar de usar Mantén, Cambia, Voltea. Mantén 1/2, cambia ÷ a ×, y voltea el divisor 1/4 a 4/1: 1/2 × 4/1 = 4/2 = 2. (Aunque aquí la respuesta casualmente es 2, dividir directamente no es una regla confiable — falla en problemas como 2/3 ÷ 1/2.)

onLevel.label: Divide each pair of fractions using Keep, Change, Flip.
onLevel.hint: For each row, calculate the quotient by dividing the whole by the piece size.
hints: The middle column already shows Keep, Change, Flip done for you — like 1/2 × 6/1 = 6/2.
Your job is the last step: simplify each product fraction to its final quotient.
Row one ends at 6/2 — divide the top by the bottom to simplify, then do the same for every row.
onLevel.explanation: The middle column has already done Keep, Change, Flip, so the last column is only the simplifying step: 6/2 = 3, 12/4 = 3, 6/3 = 2, and 20/8 = 2 1/2. Every quotient is more than 1 because each dividend holds more than one copy of its divisor.
onLevel.explanationEs: La columna del medio ya hizo Conserva, Cambia, Voltea, así que la última columna es solo el paso de simplificar: 6/2 = 3, 12/4 = 3, 6/3 = 2 y 20/8 = 2 1/2. Todos los cocientes son mayores que 1 porque cada dividendo contiene más de una copia de su divisor.
onLevel.labelEs: Divide cada pareja de fracciones usando Conserva, Cambia, Voltea.
hintsEs: La columna del medio ya muestra Conserva, Cambia, Invierte hecho por ti, como 1/2 × 6/1 = 6/2.
Tu trabajo es el último paso: simplificar cada fracción producto hasta su cociente final.
La fila uno termina en 6/2: divide el número de arriba entre el de abajo para simplificar y haz lo mismo en cada fila.

onLevel.label: Match each fraction division to its quotient.
onLevel.hint: Match each fraction division to its answer. Divide the first number by the second.
hints: Flip only the SECOND fraction in each pair, then multiply across.
Simplify every product — some matches are whole numbers, some are mixed numbers like 2 1/2.
Start with 4/5 ÷ 2/5: the denominators match, so ask how many groups of 2 fifths fit into 4 fifths.
onLevel.explanation: Flipping only the second fraction and multiplying produces every match: 4/5 × 5/2 = 2, 3/4 × 8/3 = 2, 5/6 × 3/1 = 15/6 = 2 1/2, 2/3 × 6/1 = 4, and 7/8 × 4/1 = 28/8 = 3 1/2. Only 1/2 ÷ 3/4 has a divisor larger than its dividend, which is why 2/3 is the one quotient below 1.
onLevel.explanationEs: Voltear solo la segunda fracción y multiplicar produce cada pareja: 4/5 × 5/2 = 2, 3/4 × 8/3 = 2, 5/6 × 3/1 = 15/6 = 2 1/2, 2/3 × 6/1 = 4 y 7/8 × 4/1 = 28/8 = 3 1/2. Solo 1/2 ÷ 3/4 tiene un divisor mayor que su dividendo, por eso 2/3 es el único cociente menor que 1.
onLevel.labelEs: Une cada división de fracciones con su cociente.
hintsEs: Invierte solo la SEGUNDA fracción de cada pareja y luego multiplica.
Simplifica cada producto: algunas respuestas son números enteros y otras son números mixtos como 2 1/2.
Empieza con 4/5 ÷ 2/5: los denominadores coinciden, así que pregunta cuántos grupos de 2 quintos caben en 4 quintos.

onLevel.stem: A recipe needs 2/3 cup of sugar. You only have a 1/6-cup scoop. How many scoops do you need?
choiceFeedback: Multiplying doesn't answer 'how many fit.' Divide the whole by the piece size.
The dividend (whole) goes first. The divisor (piece size) is second.
Only 2 scoops of 1/6 cup makes 2/6 = 1/3 cup — not enough sugar. Use Keep, Change, Flip on 2/3 ÷ 1/6 and simplify what you get.
hints: The recipe total is 2/3 cup; one scoop holds 1/6 cup — you're counting scoops, not multiplying.
Rewrite 2/3 in sixths so both amounts use the same size pieces.
Multiply top and bottom of 2/3 by 2 to get sixths, then count how many 1/6-scoops that makes.
onLevel.stemEs: Una receta necesita 2/3 de taza de azúcar. Solo tienes una cuchara medidora de 1/6 de taza. ¿Cuántas cucharadas necesitas?
hintsEs: El total de la receta es 2/3 de taza y una cuchara contiene 1/6 de taza: estás contando cucharadas, no multiplicando.
Reescribe 2/3 en sextos para que ambas cantidades usen piezas del mismo tamaño.
Multiplica arriba y abajo de 2/3 por 2 para obtener sextos y luego cuenta cuántas cucharadas de 1/6 forman.

onLevel.label: Place each quotient on the number line.
onLevel.hint: Solve each division. Then find the quotient on the number line.
hints: Each label shows its quotient after the equals sign — the division is already done.
The line runs 0 to 6 by ones. Watch out: two of the targets land on the same tick.
Place A first: 1/2 ÷ 1/6 = 3, so the point goes on 3. Then check which other target shares that tick.
onLevel.explanation: Each label already shows its quotient, so the work is deciding where those values sit on a line that runs 0 to 6. A and B both simplify to 3, since 1/2 × 6/1 = 3 and 3/4 × 4/1 = 3, so they share a tick; C lands on 2 and D lands on 6 because 3/4 × 8/1 = 6.
onLevel.explanationEs: Cada etiqueta ya muestra su cociente, así que el trabajo es decidir dónde caen esos valores en una recta que va de 0 a 6. A y B se simplifican a 3, ya que 1/2 × 6/1 = 3 y 3/4 × 4/1 = 3, así que comparten la misma marca; C cae en 2 y D cae en 6 porque 3/4 × 8/1 = 6.

onLevel.title: Spot the Common Mistake
onLevel.correctWork: The student changed ÷ to × but forgot to flip the divisor. Keep 2/3, change ÷ to ×, and flip the divisor 1/2 to its reciprocal 2/1: 2/3 × 2/1 = 4/3 = 1 1/3. The correct quotient is 4/3 (1 1/3), not 1/3.
hints: After you change ÷ to ×, you must also flip the second fraction (the divisor).
The divisor 1/2 should become its reciprocal 2/1 before you multiply: 2/3 × 2/1 = 4/3.
onLevel.explanation: The step that changed ÷ to × left the divisor as 1/2 instead of flipping it, so the problem turned into multiplication of the original fractions. Keep, Change, Flip turns the divisor into 2/1, giving 2/3 × 2/1 = 4/3 = 1 1/3. That size makes sense, because 1/2 is smaller than 2/3, so more than one copy fits.
onLevel.explanationEs: El paso que cambió ÷ por × dejó el divisor como 1/2 en vez de voltearlo, así que el problema se convirtió en una multiplicación de las fracciones originales. Conserva, Cambia, Voltea convierte el divisor en 2/1, lo que da 2/3 × 2/1 = 4/3 = 1 1/3. Ese tamaño tiene sentido, porque 1/2 es menor que 2/3, así que cabe más de una copia.
onLevel.correctWorkEs: El estudiante cambió ÷ a × pero olvidó voltear el divisor. Mantén 2/3, cambia ÷ a ×, y voltea el divisor 1/2 a su recíproco 2/1: 2/3 × 2/1 = 4/3 = 1 1/3. El cociente correcto es 4/3 (1 1/3), no 1/3.

extending.title: Find the Division Error
extending.correctWork: The student forgot to flip. 2/5 × 4/3 (flip the divisor 3/4 to get 4/3). Then 2/5 × 4/3 = 8/15.
hints: In 'Keep, Change, Flip' — which fraction gets flipped?
The divisor (3/4) should become its reciprocal (4/3). Did Step 2 flip the right fraction?
extending.explanation: The Keep, Change, Flip step swapped the operation but left the divisor as 3/4, so no fraction was actually flipped. The reciprocal of 3/4 is 4/3, so the problem is 2/5 × 4/3 = 8/15, not 3/10.
extending.explanationEs: El paso de Conserva, Cambia, Voltea cambió la operación pero dejó el divisor como 3/4, así que en realidad no se volteó ninguna fracción. El recíproco de 3/4 es 4/3, así que el problema es 2/5 × 4/3 = 8/15, no 3/10.
extending.correctWorkEs: El estudiante olvidó voltear. 2/5 × 4/3 (voltea el divisor 3/4 para obtener 4/3). Entonces 2/5 × 4/3 = 8/15.

extending.prompt: Is 3/4 ÷ 1/2 the same as 1/2 ÷ 3/4? Solve both and explain why or why not. What does this tell you about the order in division?
extending.sentenceFrame: 3/4 ÷ 1/2 = ___ and 1/2 ÷ 3/4 = ___. These are ___ because ___. This shows that division is ___.
extending.hint: Explain how dividing by smaller fractions produces larger quotients using a real scenario.
hints: Don't assume the two divisions match — solve each one on its own first.
Use Keep, Change, Flip on both: flip the second fraction each time, then compare the two quotients.
First one: 3/4 ÷ 1/2 → 3/4 × 2/1. Work it out, then set up 1/2 ÷ 3/4 the same way and compare.
extending.explanation: 3/4 ÷ 1/2 becomes 3/4 × 2/1 = 6/4 = 1 1/2, while 1/2 ÷ 3/4 becomes 1/2 × 4/3 = 4/6 = 2/3, so the two expressions are not equal. Swapping the dividend and the divisor flips the quotient to its reciprocal, which shows that division is not commutative — order matters.
extending.explanationEs: 3/4 ÷ 1/2 se convierte en 3/4 × 2/1 = 6/4 = 1 1/2, mientras que 1/2 ÷ 3/4 se convierte en 1/2 × 4/3 = 4/6 = 2/3, así que las dos expresiones no son iguales. Intercambiar el dividendo y el divisor convierte el cociente en su recíproco, lo que muestra que la división no es conmutativa: el orden importa.
extending.promptEs: ¿Es 3/4 ÷ 1/2 lo mismo que 1/2 ÷ 3/4? Resuelve los dos y explica por qué sí o por qué no. ¿Qué te dice esto sobre el orden en la división?
hintsEs: No supongas que las dos divisiones son iguales: resuelve primero cada una por su cuenta.
Usa Conserva, Cambia, Invierte en las dos: invierte la segunda fracción cada vez y luego compara los dos cocientes.
La primera: 3/4 ÷ 1/2 → 3/4 × 2/1. Resuélvela y luego plantea 1/2 ÷ 3/4 igual y compara.

extending.label: Divide, then check your answer by multiplying: quotient × divisor should equal the dividend.
extending.hint: As the divisor decreases, does the quotient increase or decrease? Track the pattern.
hints: Each row pairs a division with a multiplication check — the check should rebuild the dividend.
Find the quotient with Keep, Change, Flip, then multiply quotient × divisor to confirm.
Row one: 5/6 ÷ 1/3 → 5/6 × 3/1. Simplify it, then multiply your quotient by 1/3 — you should land back on 5/6.
extending.explanation: Keep, Change, Flip gives 5/6 × 3/1 = 15/6 = 5/2, 4/9 × 3/2 = 12/18 = 2/3, and 7/8 × 2/1 = 14/8 = 7/4. The check column multiplies each quotient back by its divisor — 5/2 × 1/3 = 5/6, 2/3 × 2/3 = 4/9, and 7/4 × 1/2 = 7/8 — landing on the original dividend every time.
extending.explanationEs: Conserva, Cambia, Voltea da 5/6 × 3/1 = 15/6 = 5/2, 4/9 × 3/2 = 12/18 = 2/3 y 7/8 × 2/1 = 14/8 = 7/4. La columna de comprobación multiplica cada cociente por su divisor —5/2 × 1/3 = 5/6, 2/3 × 2/3 = 4/9 y 7/4 × 1/2 = 7/8— y cae en el dividendo original cada vez.
extending.labelEs: Divide y después comprueba tu respuesta multiplicando: cociente × divisor debe ser igual al dividendo.
hintsEs: Cada fila junta una división con una comprobación por multiplicación: la comprobación debe reconstruir el dividendo.
Halla el cociente con Conserva, Cambia, Invierte y luego multiplica cociente × divisor para confirmar.
Fila uno: 5/6 ÷ 1/3 → 5/6 × 3/1. Simplifícalo y luego multiplica tu cociente por 1/3: debes regresar a 5/6.

optionalActivity.name: Fraction Operation Lockbox
optionalActivity.intro: The evidence vault is sealed — divide each pair of fractions in simplest form and use your quotients to crack every lock.

practice.commonMistake: A common mistake in Divide Fractions is flipping the wrong fraction: students flip the dividend (the first fraction) instead of the divisor (the second fraction). For example, solving 3/4 ÷ 5/8 by flipping 3/4 to 4/3 and keeping 5/8 gives 4/3 × 5/8 = 20/24 = 5/6 — but only the divisor gets flipped. Keep 3/4, change ÷ to ×, and flip only the divisor 5/8 to its reciprocal 8/5: 3/4 × 8/5 = 24/20 = 6/5. Before you submit, check that the fraction you kept (the dividend) is still facing the same way it started.

diagram.title: Board Cut Into 1/12-ft Pieces
diagram.caption: The top bar is the 5/6-ft board (same as 10/12); the bottom bar shows it split into ten equal 1/12-ft pieces, so 5/6 ÷ 1/12 = 10 pieces.

connect.scenario: A carpenter has a board that is 5/6 of a foot long. She needs to cut pieces that are each 1/12 of a foot. She wants to know how many pieces she can cut from the board.
connect.promptQuestion: How does dividing fractions help the carpenter?
connect.prompt: The carpenter can cut ___ pieces because 5/6 ÷ 1/12 = ___.

check.explanation: 5/6 = 10/12, and ten twelfths hold ten 1/12 pieces. In symbols: 5/6 × 12/1 = 60/6 = 10.
6 × 2 = 12, so multiply the top by 2 as well: 5 × 2 = 10. That gives 10/12.

check.stem: If each piece were 1/6 of a foot, how many pieces?

connect.modelAnswer: 5/6 ÷ 1/12 = 10 pieces. Rewrite 5/6 as 10/12 and count the twelfths, or multiply by the reciprocal: 5/6 × 12/1 = 60/6 = 10.

exitTicket.explanation: 5/6 ÷ 1/12 = 10. Using the reciprocal, 5/6 × 12/1 = 60/6 = 10. Since 5/6 = 10/12, ten 1/12-foot pieces fit into the board.
choiceFeedback: That multiplies 5/6 by 1/12. The question asks how many 1/12-foot pieces fit, so divide.
That is the original board length, not the number of pieces. Count how many 1/12 units make 5/6.
That flips both fractions. Keep 5/6, flip only the divisor 1/12 to 12/1, then multiply.
hints: The board is 5/6 foot long, and each piece is 1/12 foot. You are counting how many pieces fit.
Rewrite 5/6 in twelfths so the board and each piece use the same-size unit.
5/6 = 10/12. Count how many 1/12-foot pieces are in 10/12 foot.

printables.name: Divide Fractions — Color by Number
printables.desc: Solve each problem, then color by the answer to reveal a picture.
